claims.text: Pre-heating the LPBF build platform to 500°C will reduce residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi miniature components relative to a room-temperature platform.
Pre-heating the build platform to 500°C will improve the mechanical properties of LPBF AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
Using a 500°C pre-heated build platform will simplify LPBF processing of AlCrFeNiSi.
Build-platform pre-heating reduces thermal gradients during solidification.
Pre-heating reduces the temperature differential between the molten pool and surrounding material.
Reducing the molten-pool temperature differential minimizes thermal stresses.
Reducing the molten-pool temperature differential promotes formation of a more uniform microstructure.
A 500°C pre-heated platform will decrease residual thermal stress by at least 30% relative to a room-temperature platform.
A 500°C pre-heated platform will increase tensile strength by at least 15% relative to a room-temperature platform.
A 500°C pre-heated platform will reduce warping and cracking relative to a room-temperature platform.
The applicable LPBF laser-power window is 200–300 W.
The applicable LPBF scan-speed window is 800–1200 mm/s.
The applicable LPBF layer-thickness window is 30–50 µm.
The proposed processing window is limited to miniature components measuring less than 10 mm in every direction.
Tensile performance will be evaluated by room-temperature uniaxial tensile testing.
Residual stress will be measured using X-ray diffraction.
Room-temperature-platform LPBF components exhibit high residual stresses.
Room-temperature-platform LPBF components exhibit lower tensile strength.
Room-temperature-platform LPBF components exhibit frequent processing defects.
The magnitude of the predicted improvements depends on AlCrFeNiSi thermal conductivity and phase-transformation behavior.
